reviews.review:
This is a RPG that is worth a look for old-school, hardcore fans who love hard-as-nails high lethality combat and branching plots in a rough low fantasy setting of political intrigue (think Black Company, ASoIaF etc). This game is definitely not for everyone but if you can acclimatise yourself to some jank and a very rough UI you have a RPG here that will put hair on your chest.

Buy this game if you like

- Tough combat that requires thought, planning (and a little luck) to succeed in
- Choices and consequences. People betray, lie and backstab you and you are free to betray, lie and backstab in kind. You have an impressive amount of freedom in how to solve quests (and many quests can be solved alternatively via dialogue, theft and a plethora of non-combat skills).
- Enjoyed games like: ATOM, the early Fallouts, Infinity Engine rpgs, Age of Decadence, Colony Ship, Deus Ex 1, Knights of the Chalice etc

Watch out if you have a low tolerance for

- A less than friendly UI that will see you spending a long time juggling inventories 
- High difficulty that will see you making liberal use of the quickload feature. As soon as you're starting to feel badass Brian will throw an encounter in your way that humbles you.
- Tight resource management. Money, food, healing items, XP (Karma) and in some chapters even time itself is in short supply and needs to be rationed wisely. The game has a very harsh inventory system (both in items allowed and weight) that means you can only afford to carry stuff you genuinely need (weapons, bombs, healing items). Time is often not on your side and the game pushes you to move quickly. Combat itself gives no XP so you generally want to avoid unnecessary fighting and focus on completing objectives. No grinding here.
- Bugs are a thing (though Brian is lightning quick in responding and fixing these if you report them)
- A lot of mechanics are quite obscure and take time to wrap your head around. It took a while for me to realise that I have to level up companions myself (what poses a dilemma of hogging points for your main character or investing in your party). I'm still not entirely sure what the Inspired or Fatigued statuses mean.

Perhaps the most controversial feature of the game 

- Real Time with Pause (RTwP) combat. Both enemies and yourself are often killed in 1-3 attacks. While this means combat is never boring (even an encounter with a 'trash mob' can easily end in disaster) this also means that in what feels like the blink of an eye a fight can be lost. I understand why Brian did this as the later chapter sees large fights with dozens of combatants involved but fundamentally this is an RPG and not StarCraft.
- RTwP is common in plenty of RPGs (Baldur's Gate, Icewind Dale etc) but the difference here is that combat is so fast and deadly. It would be like if you played Baldur's Gate but nobody's HP ever got higher than 30. 
- This creates a realistic and tense feel (combatants die from just a few hits instead of being able to soak up 50 crossbow bolts like most games) but is also very tough on the player and makes combat something of a RNG fest. If your main character gets targeted by a gang of enemy archers a big battle can quite literally end in about four seconds.

Overall I'm very impressed with what Brian has created here. If you have a tolerance for reloading, enjoy plots where you can be a real cunning bastard and generally enjoy getting your ass kicked until you finally figure out a way to win this is the game for you. A goodway through Chapter 3 I see that each chapter is getting more and more open-ended and complex (with my decisions in previous chapters often having major ramifications for the next one). Perhaps I'm a masochist but I cannot help myself from coming back to this and pushing a little further.
